name: TesterArmy

team.summary: Founded by Oskar, Szymon, and Piotr (YC P26), building technical dev tools in public.

product.summary: TesterArmy is an agentic testing platform that runs end-to-end checks before deployment and in production using natural language, supporting web, iOS, and Android platforms, and integrating with coding agents via MCP.

market.summary: Engineering teams, developers, and QA professionals looking to automate web and mobile end-to-end testing without maintaining static scripts or selectors.

risks.risk: High token costs and execution time for full agentic test runs compared to deterministic frameworks like Playwright or Cypress.
Security and compliance hesitation regarding outsourcing authentication and critical application testing to a third-party SaaS.
Crowded competitive landscape with existing alternatives and skepticism over whether agentic E2E testing solves a primary unaddressed bottleneck.

founder_depth.why: Founders are technical, shipped an operational product accepted into YC P26, and actively engage with deep architectural and model-choice questions from engineers on HN.

shipping_evidence.why: Demonstrated active product deployment with a fully functioning CLI/MCP integration, live video/documentation, scale to 30+ teams, and open source tooling released like unbox-ai.

demand_signal.why: Strong HN launch engagement (132 points, 69 comments), scaling from 0 to 30+ teams using the product daily, and testimonials from multiple startup founders and engineers.

defensibility.why: Relies heavily on underlying foundation models and browser primitives with multiple competing agentic testing tools and straightforward copycat potential from coding assistants.

analysis.verdict_reason: Strong technical founder execution and active user traction in a hot dev tool category warrant a closer look despite defensibility concerns.
would_change_my_mind: Unit economics proving positive margins despite high token usage per test run
Data showing enterprise adoption overcoming third-party security and data-leak concerns
Clear moat beyond wrappers around foundation models and MCP primitives
